verses.text: Better a dry morsel in quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.

xrefs.text: Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.
Better is the little of the righteous than the abundance of many who are wicked.
Better to live in the desert than with a contentious and ill-tempered wife.
Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.

verses.text: A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son and share his inheritance as one of the brothers.

xrefs.text: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during harvest is a disgraceful son.
He who assaults his father or evicts his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
A king delights in a wise servant, but his anger falls on the shameful.
Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.
A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.

verses.text: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD is the tester of hearts.

xrefs.text: See, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.
I, the LORD, search the heart; I examine the mind to reward a man according to his way, by what his deeds deserve.
Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind.
A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but a man is tested by the praise accorded him.

I know, my God, that You test the heart and delight in uprightness. All these things I have given willingly and with an upright heart, and now I have seen Your people who are present here giving joyfully and willingly to You.

verses.text: A wicked man listens to evil lips; a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue.

xrefs.text: For the time will come when men will not tolerate sound doctrine, but with itching ears they will gather around themselves teachers to suit their own desires.
Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law resist them.
They are of the world. That is why they speak from the world’s perspective, and the world listens to them.
They say to the seers, “Stop seeing visions!” and to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us the truth! Speak to us pleasant words; prophesy illusions.
The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own authority. My people love it so, but what will you do in the end?

verses.text: He who mocks the poor insults their Maker; whoever gloats over calamity will not go unpunished.

xrefs.text: Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.
If I have rejoiced in my enemy’s ruin, or exulted when evil befell him—
If anyone with earthly possessions sees his brother in need, but withholds his compassion from him, how can the love of God abide in him?
On the day you stood aloof while strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gate and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were just like one of them.
Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.

verses.text: Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of a son is his father.

xrefs.text: Children are indeed a heritage from the LORD, and the fruit of the womb is His reward.
Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.
Your wife will be like a fruitful vine flourishing within your house, your sons like olive shoots sitting around your table.
God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM. This is what you are to say to the Israelites: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”

verses.text: Eloquent words are unfit for a fool; how much worse are lying lips to a ruler!

xrefs.text: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will be wicked.

I will set no worthless thing before my eyes. I hate the work of those who fall away; it shall not cling to me.

verses.text: A bribe is a charm to its giver; wherever he turns, he succeeds.

xrefs.text: Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.
Both hands are skilled at evil; the prince and the judge demand a bribe. When the powerful utters his evil desire, they all conspire together.
Do not deny justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.

verses.text: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.

xrefs.text: Hatred stirs up dissension, but love covers all transgressions.
Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.
A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends.
Of David. A Maskil. Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

verses.text: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.

xrefs.text: Those I love I rebuke and discipline. Therefore be earnest and repent.
Do not rebuke a mocker, or he will hate you; rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.
Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge.
Let the righteous man strike me; let his rebuke be an act of loving devotion. It is oil for my head; let me not refuse it. For my prayer is ever against the deeds of the wicked.
A wise son heeds his father’s discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.

verses.text: An evil man seeks only rebellion; a cruel messenger will be sent against him.

verses.text: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.

xrefs.text: He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.

Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.

verses.text: If anyone returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.

xrefs.text: In return for my love they accuse me, but I am a man of prayer.
For it is not an enemy who insults me; that I could endure. It is not a foe who rises against me; from him I could hide.
Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.
They repay me evil for good, to the bereavement of my soul.

verses.text: To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.

xrefs.text: It is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute, but any fool will quarrel.
do not bring hastily to court. Otherwise, what will you do in the end when your neighbor puts you to shame?
But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling.
and to aspire to live quietly, to attend to your own matters, and to work with your own hands, as we instructed you.
The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.

verses.text: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.

xrefs.text: Stay far away from a false accusation. Do not kill the innocent or the just, for I will not acquit the guilty.
Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, nor is depriving the innocent of justice.

verses.text: Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?

xrefs.text: The craving of the slacker kills him because his hands refuse to work.

verses.text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

xrefs.text: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.

verses.text: A man lacking judgment strikes hands in pledge and puts up security for his neighbor.

xrefs.text: He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer, but the one who hates indebtedness is secure.
My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, if you have struck hands in pledge with a stranger,
Do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts.
Take the garment of the one who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty.

verses.text: He who loves transgression loves strife; he who builds his gate high invites destruction.

xrefs.text: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.
But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.

To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.

verses.text: The one with a perverse heart finds no good, and he whose tongue is deceitful falls into trouble.

xrefs.text: The tongue also is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of his life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.
The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut out.
The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool invites destruction.
He who winks the eye causes grief, and foolish lips will come to ruin.
to the pure You show Yourself pure, but to the crooked You show Yourself shrewd.

verses.text: A man fathers a fool to his own grief; the father of a fool has no joy.

xrefs.text: The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother.
A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.

verses.text: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.

xrefs.text: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.
Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, but a good word cheers it up.
The spirit of a man can endure his sickness, but who can survive a broken spirit?
Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow brings death.
Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:

verses.text: A wicked man takes a covert bribe to subvert the course of justice.

xrefs.text: Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.
A bribe is a charm to its giver; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
Both hands are skilled at evil; the prince and the judge demand a bribe. When the powerful utters his evil desire, they all conspire together.
Do not deny justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
Your rulers are rebels, friends of thieves. They all love bribes and chasing after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, and the plea of the widow never comes before them.

verses.text: Wisdom is the focus of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.

xrefs.text: The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.

A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
Turn my eyes away from worthless things; revive me with Your word.

verses.text: A man of knowledge restrains his words, and a man of understanding maintains a calm spirit.

xrefs.text: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness.
My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly.
When words are many, sin is unavoidable, but he who restrains his lips is wise.
The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked blurts out evil.

verses.text: Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent, and discerning when he holds his tongue.

xrefs.text: If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!
The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.
Yet the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming, and who can tell him what will come after him?
As a dream comes through many cares, so the speech of a fool comes with many words.
Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
